title: Kazakh — passport-style ASCII (observed practice)
authority: No published table; modelled on observed English/passport spellings, Russian ICAO letters as the base
description: Kazakh Cyrillic names in the ASCII form seen in Kazakhstani passports and English usage: Kazakh letters folded (Ә→A, Ғ→G, Қ→K, Ң→N, Ө→O, Ұ/Ү→U, Һ→H, І→I), Ж→ZH, Х→KH, initial and post-vowel Е→YE, Ю/Я→YU/YA, final Й→Y (Назарбаев → Nazarbayev, Әлімханұлы → Alimkhanuly, Геннадий → Gennadiy).
notes: No Kazakhstan MIA transliteration table was found; status informal. The rules reproduce common passport/English spellings of public figures and athletes: Nazarbayev, Tokayev, Yeldos, Zhanibek Alimkhanuly, Ilyas Suleimenov, Dimash Kudaibergen, Kairat, Gennadiy Golovkin, Aliya.

Й is I (Kairat, Suleimenov, Kudaibergen, Abai) except in word-final -ий/-ей of Russian names, which give -iy/-ey (Gennadiy, Dmitriy, Sergey); Ь and Ъ are dropped. Final -ай/-ой also occurs as -ay/-oy (Abay).

Variants to generate: intervocalic С→SS (Kassym, Assel, Massimov, Yeleussinov) — frequent but not systematic (Asanali, Yesimov); initial Е→E (Erlan Karin); strict Russian ICAO (IU/IA, final II: Aliia, Gennadii); Ж→J (Kassym-Jomart); Қ→Q; Ғ→GH; Ң→NG; Ы→I (Sagintayev).
Applicants may ask for a specific English spelling backed by documents (foreign passport, marriage certificate), so any single scheme only approximates real passports.
ICAO §6.B lists Һ as C, apparently an error; Һ→H is used.

rules.note: final -ий/-ей of Russian names: Gennadiy, Sergey
